name_reason: Compliant fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> game-function name. domain=animate (UI animation, consistent with sibling fd2_animate_* helpers in aniui.c), descriptor=scroll_up_in_shop_dialog accurately describes the effect: scrolls the shop item-grid block UP within the mode13h framebuffer dialog area at 0xA8FCA. No Ghidra address residue. The 'shop_dialog' framing is correct even though roster/promotion select loops also call it -- those loops reuse the same shop-style item-grid widget/area; the sibling fd2_animate_scroll_down_in_shop_dialog uses the identical naming convention. Caller fd2_shop_menu_input_loop invokes it exactly when cursor-scroll_offset>5 (cursor past the bottom of the 6-item viewport), i.e. to scroll the list up to reveal the next row -- matching 'scroll_up'.
purpose: Plays the shop/roster item-grid 'scroll up' animation by shifting a 0x4A-row block upward in the mode13h framebuffer dialog area (0xA8FCA), in three paced 6-row steps plus a final 8-row jump.
logic_summary: Phase 1: loop step=0..2 -- for row=0..0x49 memmove a 0x11C-byte run up by 6 rows (dst 0xA8FCA+row*0x140, src 0xA974A+row*0x140 = dst+6*0x140); then memset the bottom 6 rows (0xAEC4A+i*0x140, 0x11C bytes) to palette 0x49; then fd2_delay_ms(10) for pacing. Phase 2: for row=0..0x47 memmove the 0x48-row block up by 8 rows (src 0xA99CA = dst+8*0x140); then memset the bottom 8 rows (0xAE9CA+i*0x140) to palette 0x49. Row stride 0x140 = mode13h scanline. Total net scroll = 3*6+8 = 0x1A rows. The forward (ascending) row iteration is safe for the up-shift because dst<src so a low-to-high copy never clobbers not-yet-read source rows (mirror sibling scroll_down iterates descending for the opposite reason). The compiler-generated __CHK(0x18) stack-probe prologue is the only thing the decompiler shows as extra 'in_stack' args; they are not real parameters.

returns.semantics: No return value; side effect is direct writes to the mode13h VGA aperture (real VGA RAM under DOS/4GW).
